cards.front: Recall a key point about Capacitors & Inductors
cards.back: Capacitance C = Q/V, measured in farads (F); a capacitor stores charge on parallel plates separated by a dielectric.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Capacitors & Inductors
cards.back: The energy stored in a capacitor is E = ½CV² = ½QV.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Capacitors & Inductors
cards.back: In an RC charging circuit, V_C rises exponentially: V_C = V_supply(1 − e^(−t/RC)).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Capacitors & Inductors
cards.back: The time constant τ = RC is the time for the capacitor to reach 63.2% of its final voltage when charging.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Capacitors & Inductors
cards.back: During discharge, V_C = V_initial × e^(−t/RC); after 5τ the capacitor is effectively fully discharged.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Capacitors & Inductors
cards.back: Inductance L is measured in henrys (H); an inductor stores energy in its magnetic field.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Capacitors & Inductors
cards.back: The energy stored in an inductor is E = ½LI².

cards.front: Recall a key point about Capacitors & Inductors
cards.back: An inductor opposes changes in current: V = L × dI/dt (back EMF).

cards.front: Recall a key point about Capacitors & Inductors
cards.back: Capacitors block DC at steady state but pass AC; inductors pass DC at steady state but oppose AC.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Capacitors & Inductors
cards.back: Dielectric material between capacitor plates increases capacitance by reducing the electric field.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Capacitors & Inductors
cards.back: Increasing plate area or decreasing plate separation increases capacitance.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Capacitors & Inductors
cards.back: Inductors in series add: L_total = L1 + L2; in parallel: 1/L_total = 1/L1 + 1/L2.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse electronics exam tips — capacitors & inductors?
cards.back: 1. For Capacitors & Inductors questions, use correct electronic symbols and terminology 2. Always show your working in calculations, including units at each step 3. For evaluation questions on Capacitors & Inductors, compare component choices and consider cost, reliability and tolerance 5. Draw circuit diagrams neatly with conventional symbols
